ov: Two species of broad-snouted crocodilian: the American alligator of the south-eastern US, and the much smaller Chinese alligator, which is critically endangered.

why.dg: Alligators can and do attack people, often when someone gets close to them or their nests.
why.et: Farmed commercially for meat and skins.
why.h: Not true hibernation, but it goes dormant through cold winters.

rg: Swamps, marshes, rivers and lakes of the south-eastern US; the Chinese alligator survives only in the Yangtze River valley.
df: Fish, turtles, birds and mammals; young alligators eat insects, snails and small fish.

cf.tip: An alligator has a broad U-shaped snout, and its lower teeth are hidden when its mouth is shut; a crocodile’s narrower snout shows them.

fx: Nest temperature decides whether eggs hatch male or female: 30 °C or cooler gives females, 34 °C or warmer gives males.
